subject: Proposal: Commit lane + credit workback for Q4 pilot
messages:
From: Sanjay Gupta <sanjay.g@clearline.io>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aisha Martins <aisha.m@clearline.io>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Initial MAP & questions on commit phasing

Laura —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Attached is a short MAP draft from our side (ClearLine_MAP_v1.pdf) that outlines a Q4 pilot leading into a production ramp. A few items we want to make sure are covered before we lock timelines:

- Commit phasing: we are comfortable with a stepped approach, but need clarity on how monthly TPM targets translate into credits/true-ups if we fall short.
- Credit/workback mechanics: our procurement prefers a simple month-to-month true-up rather than long-term escrow.
- Pricing bands: can you confirm pricing for the 3-tier ladder (pilot, early ramp, steady-state) and whether discounts are retroactive or prospective?
- Acceptance and milestone gating: we'll restrict the ramp after acceptance gates are met; please confirm what you require to sign off.

If you can sketch a conservative commit lane + a fallback (no-commit pilot -> optional ramp), we can take it to procurement. We're aiming to finalize commercial terms by Nov 5 so engineering can schedule infra.

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Gupta
Head of Platform Partnerships | ClearLine Inc
attachments: ClearLine_MAP_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Gupta <sanjay.g@clearline.io>
Cc: Aisha Martins <aisha.m@clearline.io>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP & questions on commit phasing

Sanjay —

Thanks for the MAP. I pulled together a very pragmatic commit lane and credit-workback option that keeps your procurement's preference for monthly true-ups in mind. I attached our draft (RWI_MAP_Draft_LB_20261028.pdf) but the core proposal is below so you can share quickly with your team: 

Proposal (high level):
- Phase 0 (Pilot, month 0): no financial commit, access to hosted API with standard rate limits and monitoring.
- Phase 1 (Onboarding months 1-2): optional soft commit of 150 TPM (tokens-per-minute proxy) averaged over a 30-day window. If actual TPM < 150, we apply a pro-rated credit at 25% of the delta for month 1, 15% for month 2 (workback credit on next invoice).
- Phase 2 (Ramp months 3-5): firm monthly commit steps — month 3: 300 TPM, month 4: 600 TPM, month 5+: 1,200 TPM steady-state. Missed TPM in ramp months trigger a 10% pro-rated credit for the shortfall in the following invoice.
- Pricing bands: pilot rate = $0.0025/token-equivalent, onboarding discounted by 10% (applied to usage above the soft commit), ramp and steady-state follow the published volume tiers with a 5% volume discount at 1,000 TPM+ threshold.
- Acceptance gates: 1) integration test suite pass (shared test harness), 2) latency SLO met on 95th percentile over a 7-day window, 3) quality sign-off on 3 canonical prompts. Sign-off moves customer from Phase 1 -> Phase 2.

Key commercial notes: monthly true-up (invoice credit/charge) — we invoice actual usage and then apply credit for missed committed TPM per the schedule above. No escrow by default; we can consider escrow if you want to lock credits in bridge months.

If that structure looks reasonable I can loop in finance for the exact dollar calculations and carve out a fallback clause for force majeure and significant downward traffic variance. I can be flexible on the first-month credit intensity to help you de-risk the pilot.

Next steps:
1) confirm you can accept monthly true-up credits versus escrow
2) confirm proposed TPM lane (150 -> 300 -> 600 -> 1200) or suggest alternate numbers
3) I'll get legal to translate into a short SOW/Exhibit and add the DocuSign link for signatures.

Would you be able to review with procurement this afternoon? If not, early tomorrow works for me.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, North America | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0187
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial MAP & questions on commit phasing — pricing / credit ask

Ben / Karthik —

FYI — ClearLine sent their MAP and I sketched a commit lane and credit/workback that favors monthly true-ups (see my reply to Sanjay). Can you review the proposed credit cadence and discounting before I push to procurement? Specific asks: 

- Are the credit percentages (25% M1, 15% M2, 10% ramp months) reasonable from an ARR protection POV?
- Can we support a 10% volume discount at 1,000 TPM under a 12-month commitment?
- If we stick to monthly true-up credits, we need a clear invoicing flow — Karthik, can you confirm accounting treatment and whether we should require a minimum billing floor?

I'm trying to avoid escrow given procurement's strong preference for no-escrow. Sanjay indicated a Nov 5 internal deadline.

Thanks —
Laura
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial MAP & questions on commit phasing — pricing / credit ask

Laura / Karthik —

Quick thoughts from GTM:
- Credit cadence: I'm ok with front-loading the credit (25% then 15%) for months 1-2 to remove friction, but let's limit it to two months only. After month 2 we go to the ramp credit at 10% as you suggested. We should call these "pilot protection credits" (language matters).
- Discounting: 10% at 1,000 TPM is tolerable if the commit term is 12 months and we include a standard annual true-up clause. For pilots that flip to dedicated, we should require a 60-day notice for capacity changes.
- Minimum billing floor: yes, require a $5k/mo minimum for first 3 months to avoid operational churn; can waive this for strategic pilots with RevOps approval.
- Invoicing flow: monthly invoice based on actual usage; if committed TPM > actual, apply credit on next invoice. Karthik — we'll need a simple journal entry template for credits.

I'll leave the exact percentages to Finance, but happy to keep the structure. We should avoid escrow language unless procurement insists. 

Ben
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Gupta <sanjay.g@clearline.io>

Date: 2026-10-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP & questions on commit phasing — final proposal

Sanjay / Aisha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your MAP and internal alignment here is the consolidated commercial proposal for the Q4 pilot -> ramp: 

Agreed commit lane and credits (final):
- Phase 0 (Pilot, month 0): no commit, access to hosted API.
- Phase 1 (Onboarding months 1-2): soft commit 150 TPM average. Pilot protection credits: 25% of the shortfall applied in month 2 if month 1 misses; 15% of the shortfall applied on the invoice following month 2 if month 2 misses.
- Phase 2 (Ramp months 3-5): firm monthly commits: month 3 = 300 TPM, month 4 = 600 TPM, month 5+ = 1,200 TPM. Missed ramp TPMs => 10% pro-rated credit on the following invoice.
- Pricing: pilot rate $0.0025/token-equivalent; onboarding discount 10% on usage above soft commit; volume discount 5% at 1,000 TPM provided there is a 12-month renewal term following ramp.
- Minimum billing floor: $5,000/month for the first 3 months (waivable by RevOps if required).
- Acceptance gates: integration tests, 95th pctl latency SLO (7d), quality sign-off on 3 prompts.
- Invoicing & credits: monthly invoices reflect actual usage; credits for missed committed TPM applied on the subsequent invoice as described. No escrow required.

Attachments: finalized draft SOW/Exhibit (I'll have Legal convert into an Exhibit with exact dollar math). I've included Ben and Karthik on the thread for quick approvals on the credit accounting and any minor adjustments.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you accept monthly true-ups and the $5k minimum (or request RevOps waiver) by Nov 2.
2) If accepted, we'll send a short Exhibit for signature (DocuSign link included once Legal finalizes).
3) Engineering will schedule a kickoff after signature — target kickoff week Nov 15.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the team through the acceptance gates and invoicing flow.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, North America | Redwood Inference
